scene_description: A bright office with a slatted window blind above a low wood cubby shelf, a floor lamp, a narrow white cabinet, a paneled door, a table, two wheeled chairs and a large foreground plant.
initial_target_observations: The initial reconstruction shows both chair shells and their central pedestal supports with wheeled bases, although the rear chair is partly occluded by the table. The view is wider than the reference, exposing more of the table and floor.
candidate_target_observations: In the candidate, the rear chair has a visible central post and wheeled base beneath the shell. The foreground chair shell is visible, but its support and base fall below the image boundary, preventing assessment of their connection. The candidate is more tightly cropped than the initial view.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The visible rear chair pedestal appears aligned beneath its shell, though its junction is partly obscured. The foreground chair support cannot be assessed in the candidate. The candidate retains the shelf, cabinet, lamp, door and plant arrangement, but the door appears closed and front-facing rather than presenting the angled leaf silhouette seen in the reference. The reference has two visible chair bases; the candidate crop does not show the foreground one.
new_visible_defects: The foreground chair base and much of the table are cropped out in the candidate, limiting comparison; this is a framing difference, not evidence that geometry is missing. No definite new mesh defect can be established from the images.
other_changes: The candidate viewpoint is closer and more frontal than the initial view, placing the window, shelf and door at larger image scale. It retains pale, smooth materials and a light plank floor, unlike the reference's darker, more textured floor and stronger tonal contrast. The candidate plant is cropped at the right edge; its pot is not visible. Both reconstructions show dark corner marks on the blind frame that are not apparent in the reference.

evidence.description: Both chair shells have visible central supports and black wheeled bases, with the foreground base near the lower edge.
Both chairs have visible pedestals and wheeled bases; the rear base is partly occluded by the table.
The rear chair pedestal and base are visible, while the foreground chair extends beyond the bottom edge before its support can be seen.
The dark paneled door has an angled leaf silhouette.
The gray paneled door reads as a more frontal, closed rectangle.
The wide framing shows the whole table and several legs.
Only a cropped portion of the tabletop remains in view.

uncertainty: No specific intended target is identified, so target resolution and change are unknown. Different camera framing and occlusion limit direct comparison of the chair supports and table. RGB images cannot establish actual mesh contact, collisions, hidden geometry or long-term capability.
